reference.source: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
clinicalPearls: A group of lethal skeletal dysplasias defined by extreme micromelia (very short limbs), a short trunk and severe deficiency of endochondral ossification

Type 1A (Houston-Harris) is caused by TRIP11 mutations and type 1B (Fraccaro) by SLC26A2 mutations, both autosomal recessive; type 2 (Langer-Saldino) is caused by dominant COL2A1 mutations, usually de novo
Presents prenatally or at birth with a large head, extremely short limbs, a narrow chest and hydrops or marked soft-tissue oedema
The small, poorly compliant thorax causes pulmonary hypoplasia and lethal respiratory failure in the perinatal period
Radiographs show virtually absent ossification of the vertebral bodies and sacrum, short ribs (with fractures in type 1A) and severely shortened, poorly modelled long bones
Type 2 belongs to the type II collagenopathy spectrum, at the severe end of a continuum that includes hypochondrogenesis and spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia
Diagnosis rests on the radiographic pattern, histology of the growth plate and molecular confirmation
Because the condition is lethal, care centres on accurate diagnosis, recurrence-risk counselling and compassionate perinatal support
reference.pathophysiology: Achondrogenesis is a disorder of cartilage and endochondral bone formation with several molecular causes. Type 1A involves TRIP11, encoding a Golgi protein needed for normal cartilage matrix processing. Type 1B involves SLC26A2, a sulphate transporter required to sulphate cartilage proteoglycans, so undersulphated matrix cannot support normal skeletal growth. Type 2 arises from dominant-negative mutations in COL2A1, the gene for type II collagen, the principal structural collagen of cartilage. In each case, disordered cartilage matrix prevents normal growth-plate function and ossification, producing the profound skeletal deficiency.
additionalDifferentials: Osteogenesis imperfecta type II (fractures, poor ossification)
Hypochondrogenesis (milder end of the COL2A1 spectrum)
additionalInvestigations: Detailed prenatal ultrasound and, where appropriate, fetal MRI to characterise limb, trunk and thoracic size
Postnatal or postmortem skeletal radiographs demonstrating the ossification pattern
Molecular testing of TRIP11, SLC26A2 and COL2A1 to define the subtype
Histopathology of the cartilage growth plate
Placental and fetal examination in perinatal death for diagnostic confirmation
Genetic counselling with consideration of parental carrier or gonadal mosaicism testing
redFlags: Severe pulmonary hypoplasia causing respiratory failure at birth
A markedly small thorax on prenatal imaging predicting lethality
Recurrence in a subsequent pregnancy indicating recessive inheritance or gonadal mosaicism
reference.prognosis: Achondrogenesis is generally lethal before or shortly after birth because of pulmonary hypoplasia; the value of diagnosis lies in accurate classification, recurrence-risk counselling and support for the family rather than in curative treatment.
pitfalls: Confusing it with other lethal short-limbed dysplasias without radiographic and molecular characterisation
Assuming a de novo dominant cause and understating recurrence risk in the recessive types
Not securing tissue or molecular confirmation before counselling about future pregnancies
Overlooking gonadal mosaicism as an explanation for recurrence in type 2
references: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
GeneReviews: Achondrogenesis and type II collagen disorders
management: Recognise the lethal nature of the condition and provide compassionate, comfort-focused perinatal palliative care rather than aggressive intervention
Confirm the diagnosis and subtype with skeletal radiographs and molecular testing of TRIP11, SLC26A2 and COL2A1 to guide counselling
Antenatal counselling when diagnosed prenatally, including discussion of the option of termination and planning for delivery
Bereavement support for the family after perinatal death
Genetic counselling with recurrence-risk assessment, including parental carrier testing and consideration of gonadal mosaicism
Offer prenatal or preimplantation genetic testing in future pregnancies
